_readme: Deterministic red-flag rules. These run INDEPENDENTLY of the machine
learning model and take priority over anything it predicts.
Why not let the model do this: a model can be argued out of an emergency
finding by an unusual phrasing or a thin symptom set, and this one was
trained on synthetic data with no notion of severity at all. A rule table
cannot be talked round, can be read by a clinician, and fails loudly.
Every rule cites the public guidance it comes from. Rules are deliberately
conservative: a false alarm costs a wasted trip, a miss can cost far more.
IMPORTANT: this mapping has NOT been reviewed by a clinician. It is
assembled from public patient-facing guidance for an educational project
and must be reviewed before any real-world use.
levels:
emergency — advise contacting emergency services immediately
urgent    — advise same-day medical assessment
triggers (a rule fires when ALL present trigger types match):
any_symptoms  — at least one of these canonical symptoms is reported
all_symptoms  — every one of these is reported
text_patterns — a regex matched against the user's own words, for things
the fixed symptom vocabulary cannot express
min_severity  — the reported episode severity is at least this

rules.title: Chest pain with other cardiac warning signs
rules.advice: Chest pain together with breathlessness, sweating or a racing heart can indicate a heart attack. Contact emergency services now — do not drive yourself.

rules.title: Severe chest pain
rules.advice: Severe chest pain needs immediate assessment. Contact emergency services now.

rules.title: Chest pain described as crushing or radiating
rules.advice: Chest pain described this way can indicate a heart attack. Contact emergency services now.

rules.title: Possible signs of a stroke
rules.advice: Sudden weakness on one side, drooping of the face, slurred speech or confusion can indicate a stroke. Contact emergency services immediately — treatment is time critical.

rules.title: Stroke described in your own words
rules.advice: These can be signs of a stroke. Contact emergency services immediately — treatment is time critical.

rules.title: Severe difficulty breathing
rules.advice: Severe difficulty breathing needs immediate assessment. Contact emergency services now.

rules.title: Unable to breathe or speak in full sentences
rules.advice: Being unable to breathe properly is a medical emergency. Contact emergency services now.

rules.title: Loss of consciousness
rules.advice: Loss of consciousness needs urgent assessment. Contact emergency services now.

rules.title: Possible severe allergic reaction
rules.advice: Swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat with difficulty breathing can be anaphylaxis. Use an adrenaline auto-injector if you have one and contact emergency services immediately.

rules.title: Severe or uncontrolled bleeding
rules.advice: Heavy bleeding that will not stop is a medical emergency. Apply firm pressure and contact emergency services now.

rules.title: Possible meningitis
rules.advice: Fever with a stiff neck can indicate meningitis, especially alongside a rash, severe headache or dislike of bright light. Seek emergency care immediately.

rules.title: Rash that does not fade under pressure
rules.advice: A rash that does not fade when pressed with a glass can indicate meningococcal infection. Seek emergency care immediately.

rules.title: Possible sepsis
rules.advice: A high temperature with confusion, slurred speech or severe breathlessness can indicate sepsis, which needs immediate treatment. Seek emergency care now.

rules.title: Sepsis warning signs described
text_patterns: not (passed |produced )?urine (all day|for a day|in a day)
rules.advice: These can be signs of sepsis, which needs immediate treatment. Seek emergency care now.

rules.title: Sudden severe neurological symptoms
rules.advice: A sudden severe headache, seizure or sudden loss of vision needs emergency assessment. Contact emergency services now.

rules.title: Thoughts of self-harm or suicide
rules.advice: You deserve support right now. Contact your local emergency services or a suicide prevention helpline immediately — in the UK, call 999 or Samaritans on 116 123. You do not have to face this alone.

rules.title: Severe abdominal pain
rules.advice: Severe abdominal pain should be assessed today. Contact your doctor or an urgent care service — go to an emergency department if it worsens, or if you also have a fever, vomiting or blood in your stool.

rules.title: Blood in stool or urine
rules.advice: Blood in your stool should be assessed promptly. Arrange to see a doctor today.

rules.title: High fever that is not settling
rules.advice: A high temperature lasting five days or more should be assessed by a doctor.

rules.title: Signs of significant dehydration
rules.advice: Dehydration with dizziness or confusion should be assessed today, especially if you cannot keep fluids down.
